extracted.intended_audience: college and university administrators, scholars, academic leaders, and humanities-focused organizations seeking Mellon funding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and priorities for Mellon Foundation Higher Learning grantmaking: who the program supports, the types of projects funded, and the Foundation's general invitation-based grantmaking process. Useful for institutions and scholars considering or preparing to pursue Mellon support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible recipients — colleges and universities
rubrics_metrics.description: Colleges and universities exploring new directions in humanistic study in a range of learning environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page explicitly lists colleges and universities as recipients and highlights openness to varied learning environments (examples elsewhere on the page include rural universities, tribal colleges, HBCUs). This signals that degree-granting institutions pursuing innovative humanistic study are a target for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible recipients — scholars and academic leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholars and academic leaders working to deepen our understanding of American history and culture, advance new methods for scholarly interpretation, and elevate underrepresented perspectives in academia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes support for individual scholars or academic leaders whose work addresses U.S. history/culture, methodological innovation in interpretation, and the elevation of underrepresented academic perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible recipients — humanities-focused organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Humanities-focused organizations committed to expanding public understanding and appreciation of the liberal arts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non‑university organizations with public-facing humanities missions are explicitly within scope when they demonstrate commitment to public understanding and appreciation of the liberal arts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of activities funded
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic research, curricular development, extracurricular programming, internships, and community partnerships are among the activities Mellon funds to broaden opportunities in the humanities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation funds a range of programmatic activities across teaching, research, student experiences, and community engagement — applicants should align proposals to one or more of these activity types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for projects beyond colleges and universities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation also funds humanities projects beyond colleges and universities that deepen understanding of the United States, its cultures, and people, and help ensure the breadth of stories told and studied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals willingness to fund non‑academic projects that advance knowledge about U.S. culture and diversify narratives; proposals should demonstrate how they expand or deepen national cultural understanding or storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority on elevating underrepresented perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects and scholars that elevate underrepresented perspectives in academia are a stated focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should show how their work centers or amplifies underrepresented voices or perspectives in the humanities; this is a programmatic priority rather than a neutral preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on diverse institutional contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: The page cites rural universities, tribal colleges, HBCUs, and more as included examples of institutions the Foundation supports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates an inclusion emphasis across institutional types and geographies; applicants from or partnering with such institutions should foreground that context in proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation-based grantmaking process
rubrics_metrics.description: Our staff seek out and get to know innovative organizations, scholars, and creators before inviting them to submit a proposal for funding. Most Mellon grants are made through these invitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural expectation: the Foundation commonly funds via invitation after staff cultivation, implying unsolicited or open applications are less common; prospective applicants should anticipate relationship-building and possible staff outreach rather than a fully open-call process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships that expand the definition of education and learning
rubrics_metrics.description: We partner with institutions that are expanding the definition of education and learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for projects or institutional partners that propose novel or broadened conceptions of education (e.g., nontraditional curricula, community-integrated learning); proposals should articulate how they rethink or extend conventional educational models.
